name: Lithuania
summary: Children, the spouse and dependent parents are guaranteed half of their intestate share. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Lithuania has no common-law trust; whether foundations can hold family wealth was not confirmed.
reserved_share: Children (including adopted), spouse, and parents who were financially dependent on the deceased: half of their intestate share (Civil Code, Book V; e-Justice cites no article). The will can leave more.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Lithuania is not in the HCCH table for the 1985 Trusts Convention. The Civil Code has a narrower trust concept than the common-law trust, per an academic thesis. Foundations: the Philea profile was not readable on private-benefit rules.
open_questions: Civil Code article numbers for the reserved share and the trust concept were not captured.
Whether private-benefit foundations are allowed was not confirmed (Philea profile snippet cut off).
The Civil Code trust concept comes from one thesis snippet.
